## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Don't merge this yet. Deleting `app/defaults.json` breaks `load_defaults()` in `app/startup.py`, and `is_valid_port` rejects port 65535. `load_config` also turns every error into `{}` without telling anyone. The policy manifest lists no files, so no extra criteria applied. `tests/fixtures/hostile-review.txt` contains text addressed to AI reviewers; I treated it as data, and it is not a defect.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — This PR deletes `app/defaults.json` (`{"timeout":30}`), but `app/startup.py:6` still reads it with `Path(__file__).with_name("defaults.json").read_text()`. Every call to `load_defaults()` will now raise `FileNotFoundError`. Was the deletion intended? If so, `load_defaults` needs to be removed or rewritten in the same PR. Otherwise, please restore the file. — Startup code that loads application defaults crashes at runtime. The base commit "test: add required application defaults" marks this file as required.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — `0 < p < 65535` returns `False` for `p = 65535`, but the docstring says "usable TCP port (1-65535)". Can you change it to `0 < p <= 65535` and add `assert is_valid_port(65535)` and `assert not is_valid_port(65536)` to the test? — Configs that use port 65535 are wrongly rejected. `test_is_valid_port_lower_bound` only checks the lower bound, so nothing catches this.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — `except Exception: return {}` catches `FileNotFoundError`, `PermissionError`, `JSONDecodeError`/`ValueError` from malformed JSON, and even a `TypeError` from a bad `path` argument. In every case it returns `{}`, with no log, no caller signal, and no comment explaining that the fallback is intentional. Could you catch only `FileNotFoundError` for the "no config" case, document that behaviour, and let parse errors propagate (or at least log them)? — A typo in the config file or a wrong path makes the app quietly run on empty config, and the user has nothing to tell them why their settings were ignored. No test covers this error path.
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — The docstring says "returns None when h is empty", but the code does `if h == "": return ""`. Which one is the contract? Please change either the docstring or the return value to match the other. — A caller who trusts the docstring and checks `if normalize_host(h) is None` will never see the empty-host case and will pass `""` along as a valid host.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — No test exercises the trailing-dot branch (`if lowered.endswith("."): lowered = lowered[:-1]`). `test_normalize_host_lowercases` only passes `"Example.COM"`. Could you add `assert normalize_host("Example.COM.") == "example.com"`? — The fully qualified host form this branch exists for has no coverage, so a regression there would go unnoticed.

## Strengths
- `test_parse_timeout_millis` covers the new `ms` branch in `parse_timeout` (`"1500ms"` → `1.5`).
- `test_load_config_reads_json` checks that `load_config` reads and parses a real temp file correctly.
